column1: # The dates the eval's 20 lectures carry, and where they came from.
# THESE DATES ARE CONSTRUCTED. THEY ARE NOT MIT'S CALENDAR.
# MIT OCW publishes 6.006 Spring 2020's lecture notes and its topic titles. It
# does not publish, anywhere this project found, the calendar date each lecture
# was delivered. So the dates below are invented: lecture N sits in the Nth
# Tue/Thu slot counting from Tue 2020-02-04, with nothing skipped for holidays,
# reading week, or the mid-March point at which MIT actually went remote.
# They are stored with `occurred_at_source = manual`, which is the truthful
# value -- a person chose them -- and not `parsed_syllabus`, which would claim a
# source said something it never said.
# Why inventing them is defensible here, stated so it is not mistaken for
# sloppiness: the eval reads *order*, never distance. `build_timeline` badges the
# earliest `occurred_at` and draws no proportional axis -- the timeline is an
# ordering, not a scale. Every strictly increasing assignment keyed to the
# lecture ordinal therefore produces a byte-identical tally, and this one is
# strictly increasing with no ties. The scores do not depend on these dates.
# Why it still has to be flagged at every citation: "20 MIT 6.006 lectures dated
# 2020-02-04 to 2020-04-09" reads as archival fact, and it is not one. Anyone
# quoting the eval's 2/16 or 4/16 must be one hop from this file. Zero dated
# documents was not an option -- it would score every question `unrankable` and
# leave the phase's headline claim unmeasured -- so the choice was between
# constructed dates that are labelled and no measurement at all.
# The one thing here that IS real is the order: lecture 7 did precede lecture 8.
# That is the only property the eval consumes.
# Reversal condition: real 6.006 Spring 2020 lecture dates, from OCW or a
# syllabus. They would not change any number in the eval. They would change what
# this corpus can be used to demonstrate later -- a proportional axis, a gap, a
# "you learned this three weeks before the exam" claim -- none of which this
# corpus can support today.
# Applied by `python evals/date_corpus.py <course_id>`.
# ordinal<TAB>occurred_on
